mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) contraction of more than 10% signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate earnings and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST < previous year - 10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 8% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for four consecutive months signals a broad-based contraction in economic output, which reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > -1% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% while consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) remains below 1% signals a front-loaded policy tightening in a low-inflation environment, which raises real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4.5% AND CPIAUCSL < 101 (i.e., < 1%) in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real personal income (PAYEMS) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months signals weakening household purchasing power, which reduces demand for goods and services and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS falls > -0.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the unemployment rate above 7% and a fall in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 1% in the same month signals a sharp labor market deterioration, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 7% AND PAYEMS falls > -1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) of more than 0.3% for five consecutive months signals a protracted weakening in aggregate demand, which consistently reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, regardless of monetary policy stance.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
